channel.title: The Resource Library — CheapInfra #share-tech + #providers
channel.description: A curated, browsable archive of 277 developer resources shared in the CheapInfra Discord's #share-tech and #providers channels, newest first.

item.title: Isoquant
item.description: A new PAYGO inference provider launching with GLM-5.3-Flash at $0.07/$0.20 per 1M input/output tokens with automatic prompt caching; drop-in OpenAI-compatible API, no top-up fees. Its published benchmarks claim the lowest latency and highest throughput versus Together, CoreWeave, Baseten, Fireworks, and Z.ai. Pricing and benchmark figures are vendor-reported and not independently verified. — shared by thelaggingway in #providers.

item.title: Prism Inference
item.description: Pay-as-you-go inference with no minimums across serverless, elastic, private and dedicated endpoints, plus batch. Lists per-model rates (GLM-5.3 $1.40/$4.40, Kimi K3 $3/$15 per 1M tokens) and states strict zero data retention — inputs and outputs are never used for training. — shared by thelaggingway in #providers.

item.title: InferHub
item.description: Proxy service that pools AI subscriptions into one API. Shared as "a rly interesting proxy" with per-plan pricing on its site. — shared by one_phantomic in #providers.

item.title: AIHubMix
item.description: Multi-model API with per-model pricing, including a GLM 5.3 coding endpoint. Shared via its GLM 5.3 API pricing page. — shared by one_phantomic in #providers.

item.title: Surplus Intelligence
item.description: OpenAI-compatible inference marketplace that routes each request to the cheapest current offer. Vendor claims ~38% savings via routing; pricing and retention terms weren't independently verified. — shared by Felix in #providers.

item.title: Kitani
item.description: Open inference on independent hardware with a prepaid USD balance — the max request cost is reserved, then settled on completion. API is OpenAI-compatible at api.kitani.ai/v1. — shared by rah in #providers.

item.title: Pareto Inference
item.description: Pay-per-token inference running on Pareto's own GPUs, including GLM 5.3 Flash. Shared via its pricing page. — shared by Rykuuun in #providers.

item.title: BytePlus ModelArk
item.description: BytePlus's Coding Plan for Claude Code, Cursor, Cline, Kilo Code, Roo Code and OpenCode, covering models like Dola-Seed-2.0-pro, GLM-5.1 and DeepSeek V4. Exact plan prices weren't visible on the promo page. — shared by Rykuuun in #providers.

item.title: Parasail
item.description: Inference provider whose homepage FAQ states explicit zero data retention alongside SLA terms. Surfaced in #providers via a comparisons board post. — shared by tom (App) in #providers.

item.title: Inceptron
item.description: Inference provider with ISO 27001 certification, GDPR compliance and EU residency. No zero-retention statement was found on its site. — shared by tom (App) in #providers.

item.title: Subconscious
item.description: Coding plans starting at $100/mo with 60M tokens/day. Shared via its pricing page. — shared by Tom in #providers.

item.title: FEIHOA
item.description: Unlimited AI plans from €6. States prompts and outputs are not used for training, though it may retain data briefly for security, abuse prevention and legal reasons. — shared by Tom in #providers.

item.title: Crof
item.description: Inference provider at crof.ai; public evidence is thin (snippet-based). Third-party substitution allegations seen during research are unverified and not repeated here. — shared by tom (App) in #providers.

item.title: Real API Pricing
item.description: GitHub repo behind the real-api-pricing comparison of actual inference API prices. Its web app is already in this library's web-apps section; this is the distinct source repo. — shared by JohnDotOwl in #providers.

item.title: OpenCode Go
item.description: Subscription plan for the OpenCode coding agent. Shared with a screenshot of the plan page. — shared by UT in #providers.

item.title: SingularityAPI
item.description: Inference API; a forwarded announcement noted DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash going live on it. — shared by uur in #providers.

item.title: DeepSeek clock
item.description: Personal utility page showing DeepSeek's live peak/off-peak status in local time with both models' prices either way. Rates match the official docs. — shared by Alp in #providers.

item.title: Token Harbor
item.description: Inference API with a published pricing page; the sharer noted roughly 3.5x markup on its $10 plan. — shared by thelaggingway in #providers.

item.title: StreamLake
item.description: Kuaishou's AI cloud / model-as-a-service platform with API and SDK integration for online inference. Holds ISO 27001/27017/42001 and MLPS Level 3; no explicit zero-retention statement found. — shared by tom (App) in #providers.

item.title: CoreWeave
item.description: GPU cloud infrastructure company offering serverless inference APIs, dedicated endpoints and GPU clusters. Infrastructure rather than a retail model API. — shared by tom (App) in #providers.

item.title: GMI Cloud
item.description: GPU cloud with serverless inference APIs and dedicated endpoints; lists H100 at $2/GPU-hour and H200 at $2.60/GPU-hour. — shared by tom (App) in #providers.

item.title: Venice
item.description: Private AI chat and API with free entry and paid tiers (Pro $18/mo). Its API carries a zero-data-retention promise. — shared by tom (App) in #providers.

item.title: Relace
item.description: Coding-focused API (Instant Apply model, code retrieval, embeddings, reranking) rather than general LLM inference. Available via Continue.dev, with a self-host/VPC option. — shared by tom (App) in #providers.

item.title: AntSeed
item.description: Open market for AI inference with no account or email required and optional TEE-backed providers. That design is not the same as a universal zero-retention promise. — shared by Tom in #providers.

item.title: Inco
item.description: Recently launched its own inference platform, announced on the company blog. — shared by Tom in #providers.

item.title: Kenari
item.description: Indonesian inference API — one API key, paid in Rupiah. Shared via its pricing page. — shared by ROman in #providers.

item.title: InferenceSaver
item.description: Comparison and routing service claiming 40–80% savings on AI inference costs. — shared by Rykuuun in #providers.

item.title: Nube
item.description: Inference API with published per-token pricing. States explicit zero data retention with an upstream no-training clause. — shared by baanish in #providers.

item.title: Cline Pass
item.description: Subscription for Cline's coding agent at $9.99/mo, positioned as 2–5x the quota versus direct API spend. The "5x cheaper than API" phrasing seen in chatter is not verified. — shared by linker in #providers.

item.title: Nebius Token Factory
item.description: Nebius's pay-per-token hosted inference for open text/vision models (~23 models incl. DeepSeek, Llama, Qwen). New accounts get trial credit; uses separate v1 API credentials. — shared by ajthemacboy in #providers.

item.title: Coral Bricks
item.description: High-throughput inference aimed at agents. A forwarded promo code (SUPERINT) covered GLM 5.2 and Kimi K3. — shared by scarywood75 in #providers.

item.title: Fast Inference
item.description: Gateway for AI models and coding agents with provider failover. $9/mo gives $10 gateway credit, $49/mo gives $60, then pay-as-you-go at direct rates. — shared by baanish in #providers.

item.title: Entrim
item.description: $10 in credits plus pay-as-you-go inference. Processes prompts and outputs in RAM only and does not train on them. — shared by Tom in #providers.

item.title: Merge Gateway
item.description: Multi-provider gateway. A Discord-shared "75% off DeepSeek V4 Flash through September 30" promo was not corroborated on its site. — shared by 0xSaiya in #providers.

item.title: sference
item.description: Managed inference for open models on European GPUs. Public evidence is snippet-based; details unverified. — shared by scarywood75 in #providers.

item.title: Unifically
item.description: Pay-per-use multi-model API (no subscription) with a $0.20 free balance and per-generation pricing, e.g. $0.03 per image. The sharer called it "sus" — treat vendor claims cautiously. — shared by scarywood75 in #providers.

item.title: Reflex
item.description: Post-trained Kimi K3 served with 6x context at a claimed 490 tokens/sec. Performance claims come from the provider's own page. — shared by Alp in #providers.

item.title: OpenModels
item.description: "The open market for AI tokens", with published plans. — shared by Rykuuun in #providers.

item.title: OpenRouter
item.description: Multi-provider model gateway charging a 5.5% fee, with 50 free requests/day. Shared via its GLM 5.3 provider/pricing page. — shared by scarywood75 in #providers.

item.title: TensorX
item.description: EU-hosted pay-as-you-go inference whose pricing page states verbatim: "all inference is zero data retention." — shared by Alp in #providers.

item.title: AI Router
item.description: Swiss-hosted inference API ("All of AI. One API. Made in Switzerland") with GDPR compliance and data hosted in Switzerland. Flat CHF 39/mo unlimited under a fair-use policy; OpenAI-compatible at api.airouter.ch/v1. — shared by thelaggingway in #providers.

item.title: B.AI
item.description: Inference API documented with DeepSeek-V4-Flash endpoints. — shared by Tom in #providers.

item.title: OrcaRouter
item.description: Zero-markup BYOK router with an open-source self-hostable Lite (MIT); the hosted plan includes free credits. Pass-through per-token pricing, e.g. DeepSeek V4 Flash $0.15/$0.29 per 1M in/out. — shared by simply soy in #providers.

item.title: OpenFerence
item.description: Inference API at openference.ai; public evidence is snippet-based only. A Discord claim that its GLM 5.2 "is not even real" is unverified. — shared by Tom in #providers.

item.title: wafer
item.description: Inference provider, with DeepSeek V4 Flash mentioned on it in later chatter. Surfaced via an X post from @wafer_ai. — shared by baanish in #providers.

item.title: Fireworks AI
item.description: Serverless inference from $0.10/1M tokens (under 4B params), $1 free starter credit, 50% off batch. 100–400+ open models with an OpenAI-compatible API, FireAttention engine, LoRA/RFT fine-tuning and dedicated GPUs. — shared by baanish in #providers.

item.title: RunInfra
item.description: Inference provider; its DeepSeek V4 Flash $0.13/M input price was corroborated. A "1.8¢/M blended" figure seen in chatter is not a list price. — shared by Aditya Borkar in #providers.

item.title: Freebuff
item.description: Free, ad-supported coding agent (CLI, desktop, web, cloud, chat) powered by open models like DeepSeek V4 Pro/Flash and MiniMax M3. Explicit no-training stance — it doesn't share data with third parties that would train on it. — shared by Rykuuun in #providers.

item.title: GripHubRouter
item.description: Cheap pay-as-you-go multi-model router, reportedly built by the sharer's friend. — shared by Febryan in #providers.

item.title: Melious
item.description: EU-hosted pay-as-you-go inference; the sharer cited ~240 tok/s on DeepSeek V4 Flash. States it does not train on user data. — shared by Sewer56 in #providers.

item.title: SiliconFlow
item.description: One OpenAI-compatible API for open and commercial LLMs with serverless pay-as-you-go and dedicated endpoints. Homepage claim: "No data stored, ever." — shared by thelaggingway in #providers.

item.title: CheaperInference
item.description: Pay-as-you-go inference with published example rates. Prompt and response bodies are not logged, with zero data retention on supported routes. — shared by 0xSaiya in #providers.

item.title: Novita
item.description: Inference provider, mentioned as a fan-out target in routing chatter. — shared by kenn in #providers.

item.title: Command Code
item.description: GOAT plan — $10/mo for $70 in credits (limits $14/5h, $35/week, $70/month) across 30+ open and closed models. No zero-retention statement found. — shared by Alp in #providers.

item.title: DeepSeek
item.description: DeepSeek's official API pricing: pay-as-you-go with 50% off-peak discounts (Flash $0.15/$0.60, Pro $0.66/$1.98 per 1M in/out on cache miss; peak is 2x). The $0.13/$0.30 figures seen in Discord are stale. — shared by Sewer56 in #providers.

item.title: YOLO Auto
item.description: Unlimited-token API plans, currently $19/$39 — the Discord-era $6/mo claim is superseded. Shared as an unlimited Qwen3.6-35B API. — shared by Rykuuun in #providers.

item.title: Claudin.io
item.description: Flat-rate API keys for coding agents, $9–$99. — shared by Rykuuun in #providers.

item.title: regolo.ai
item.description: European inference platform with EUR per-token pay-as-you-go (e.g. Llama-3.3-70B €0.60/€2.70 per 1M in/out) and 70% off the first 3 months. Marketing claim: "Zero data retention on European green infrastructure." — shared by Rykuuun in #providers.

item.title: Arli AI
item.description: Inference API with unlimited-request plans and an explicit zero-logging statement. The sharer noted it seemed new and unstable. — shared by Rykuuun in #providers.

item.title: Hetzner
item.description: Hetzner's free experimental open-weight LLM inference API (announced July 2026), EU-hosted. Roughly 4M input / 100k output tokens per 60s per key, no SLA — not for production. — shared by baanish in #providers.

item.title: Synthetic
item.description: Inference provider; a forwarded announcement covered its scaling of Kimi K3. — shared by baanish in #providers.

item.title: Aster
item.description: OpenAI-compatible inference with free, Pro and Max tiers. States zero data retention on the free tier; Pro around $20 for $30 in tokens. — shared by scarywood75 in #providers.

item.title: Featherless
item.description: Open-model inference provider. Only its status page was visible during research. — shared by whaaaat in #providers.

item.description: Meituan's LongCat with Token Packs — 50M tokens for $4.90 (promotion corroborated). Surfaced via an X post. — shared by asx in #providers.

item.title: DeepInfra
item.description: Pay-as-you-go inference across 100+ models with explicit zero data retention. Example: GLM-5.3 Flash $0.075/$0.25 per 1M. — shared by Alp in #providers.

item.title: CheapestInference
item.description: Flat-rate unlimited time-block subscriptions — Core pool from $22/mo per 8-hour daily block, Frontier $71/mo, Flagship $199/mo. Prompts and completions are processed in memory and discarded, never used for training. — shared by tushii in #providers.

item.title: PrivacyWatch
item.description: Open-source comparison of 86+ provider families (97 surfaces) on training, retention, zero-retention and data location, quoting each provider's own ToS and privacy docs. Maintained by the same crew as this library. — shared by thelaggingway in #providers.

item.title: OpenAI API pricing
item.description: OpenAI's official per-1M-token pricing page (e.g. gpt-6-luna $0.10 in / $0.50 out short-context). Useful as the first-party reference behind third-party price comparisons. — shared by simply soy in #providers.

item.title: Zro
item.description: $20/mo including $60 of inference spend, OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible. Explicit zero request retention — prompts and completions are never used for training, evaluation or analytics. — shared by Tom in #providers.

item.title: InferX
item.description: Pay-as-you-go inference across 200+ one-click production-ready model endpoints. — shared by thelaggingway in #providers.

item.title: xKiro
item.description: Unified gateway — free tier with 40+ free models and 5M tokens/day (no card), pay-as-you-go about 35% below official prices on select models. 90+ models across 16 providers on one API key. — shared by thelaggingway in #providers.

item.title: StepFun
item.description: StepFun's open platform with a usage-billed API (api.stepfun.ai/v1) and a 15-day trial needing no card. Serves Step 5 Preview and StepAudio 3. — shared by thelaggingway in #providers.

item.title: Phoenix Grove
item.description: Coding-plan provider; the sharer noted a vague allowance but a free month on offer. — shared by thelaggingway in #providers.

item.title: Neuralwatt
item.description: $10/kWh pay-as-you-go (or per-token), $1 free credit after adding a payment method; monthly plans $20–$200. Hosted multi-model OpenAI-compatible API plus on-prem deployment; 14 models. — shared by Blessed Piss Enjoyer in #providers.

item.title: Chutes
item.description: Inference provider that was notably early serving Kimi K3, per channel chatter. — shared by thelaggingway in #providers.

item.title: Telnyx
item.description: Inference API with published per-token pricing — Kimi K3 at $2.70/M input, $0.27/M cached input, $13.50/M output. The sharer noted they're open to negotiating volume pricing. — shared by thelaggingway in #providers.

item.title: Charm Hyper
item.description: Free monthly credits plus a $20/mo plan, with an explicit zero-data-retention and GDPR claim. — shared by Alp in #providers.

item.title: TokenWatch
item.description: Live price comparison across inference providers, maintained by the same crew as this library. The sharer noted a Hyper subscription yields $12.50 of inference a day. — shared by thelaggingway in #providers.

item.title: Zyloo
item.description: Subscription-based inference provider at zyloo.io. — shared by thelaggingway in #providers.

item.title: Moonshot platform docs
item.description: Moonshot AI's platform documentation for the Kimi model family. Shared originally via a Kimi-K3 Hugging Face link. — shared by Manar in #providers.

item.title: Verboo Code
item.description: Free trial, then unlimited-token subscriptions from Junior $24/mo to Ultra $269/mo, plus a usage API from $0.12/1M input tokens. Coding agent plus OpenAI-compatible API on Brazilian servers; states it does not train on or review code and calls. — shared by thelaggingway in #providers.

item.title: Makora
item.description: Inference provider and optimization service — Starter $20/mo and Developer $200/mo (both shown sold out), with private model serving and on-prem options. Starter covers unlimited models under 40B parameters. — shared by 0xSaiya in #providers.

item.title: Railway Changelog #0309: Free VMs without an account
item.description: Railway Changelog #0309 opens free Linux VMs with no account: `ssh railway.new` gets a 2 vCPU/2 GB box with coding agents preinstalled, 60 minutes to build and 24 hours to claim it before deletion. The same edition adds request tracing in Priority Boarding (edge-to-database waterfalls with no code changes) and OpenCode on Cloud Agents for persistent agent VMs. — shared by baanish in #share-tech.

item.title: Orca
item.description: A free, open-source Agent Development Environment (ADE): run Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor CLI, and other CLI agents in parallel across isolated git worktrees, with a Ghostty-class terminal, in-app diff review, embedded browser, and SSH dev built in. Bring your own subscriptions — agents run side by side without interfering. — shared by ROman in #share-tech.

item.title: heddlework
item.description: A native, harness-neutral workspace for agent sessions: task graphs, diffs, and durable work across coding agents — Pi first, Codex and Claude next. Very early (~12 stars); expect rough edges. — shared by Aspiring UBI Recipient in #share-tech.

item.title: paseo.sh
item.description: A free, open-source (Apache 2.0) self-hosted daemon for running Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, OpenCode, and Pi from anywhere — phone, desktop, or web. Agents run on your own machine with your own credentials; optional end-to-end encrypted relay, MCP/CLI/TypeScript SDK, and local-first voice. — shared by ROman in #share-tech.

item.title: gpui-kit
item.description: Rust GUI components for building cross-platform desktop apps on GPUI (the framework behind Zed). ~14.8k stars — one of the more-starred GPUI component libraries. — shared by thelaggingway in #share-tech.

item.title: scenario-labs/skills
item.description: Agent skills for Scenario: image, video, audio, texture, 3D, and custom-model workflows over the Scenario MCP, aimed at games, entertainment, and creative verticals. Installs with `npx skills add scenario-labs/skills`; ~450 stars. — shared by thelaggingway in #share-tech.

item.title: Detail
item.description: A curated gallery of the small UI decisions that make products feel considered — smarter word breaks, corner-morph animations, name-derived placeholders — each shown as a short clip. Curated by Rene Wang; a good reference for stealing micro-interaction ideas. — shared by Rykuuun in #share-tech.

item.title: Landbook
item.description: A website design inspiration gallery with a large curated collection of landing pages, e-commerce sites, portfolios, and templates, plus boards for saving references. Useful for browsing real-world site design by category. — shared by Rykuuun in #share-tech.

item.title: MaxiBestOf
item.description: A website design and typography inspiration feed updated every weekday, pairing featured sites with their font stacks (e.g., Geist, Neue Haas Grotesk). A Pro tier adds private collections and HD screenshots. — shared by Rykuuun in #share-tech.

item.title: SoulStack
item.description: ProxySoul × Empryo: a bundle of skills, agents, an "immune system," and habits for coding agents. Very early (~17 stars); concept-heavy and expect rough edges. — shared by thelaggingway in #share-tech.

item.title: GLiNER2.5-Decide
item.description: Fastino's 340M-parameter open-weight model for schema-defined decision-making: feed it text plus typed questions and get valid answers with probabilities, confidence scores, and constraint-feasibility metadata. Apache 2.0, CPU-capable, strong on routing/triage/guardrail tasks. Benchmark figures are vendor-reported and not independently verified. — shared by Tom in #share-tech.

item.title: pi-warden
item.description: Guardrails for Pi built on pi-typesafe — "steer the agent instead of interrupting you: Jev judges." Part of a small Pi-safety ecosystem from the same author as the next entry. — shared by Aspiring UBI Recipient in #share-tech.

item.title: pi-typesafe
item.description: TypeSafe decisions for Pi — a batched evaluation tool, terminal playground and typed API for extensions. The foundation pi-warden builds on. — shared by Aspiring UBI Recipient in #share-tech.

item.title: BrokenArXiv / ArXivMath (announcement)
item.description: Jasper Dekoninck releasing new versions of the BrokenArXiv and ArXivMath benchmarks. Announcement only; useful pointer for anyone tracking eval benchmarks. — shared by Rykuuun in #share-tech.

item.title: Arrow 2 (announcement)
item.description: QuiverAI's Arrow 2 — their latest models for generating precise, editable vector graphics. Announcement only; a notable data point in AI vector-graphics generation. — shared by Rykuuun in #share-tech.

item.title: MiniCPM5-2B-PCD
item.description: MiniCPM5 2B PCD weights on Hugging Face — the same model family as the 16 Sept in-browser Pi announcement. The model behind that WebGPU coding-agent demo. — shared by Tom in #share-tech.

item.title: pi-claude-agent-sdk
item.description: An inference provider that lets Pi (a terminal agent harness) run on Claude Code Pro/Max subscriptions instead of API keys. Kenn is using a fork and admits he "just closed my eyes and let the agent figure it out" — expect rough edges. — shared by kenn in #share-tech.

item.title: pi-claude-bridge
item.description: Lets you route Pi's model calls through a Claude subscription ("allow sub usage in pi"). Same cost-saving idea as pi-claude-agent-sdk: agentic coding without per-token API billing. — shared by kenn in #share-tech.

item.title: spirula-studio
item.description: Cross-vendor 3D Gaussian Splatting trainer — video to splat to mesh, running on Vulkan or CUDA. Notable for not being CUDA-locked. — shared by Tom in #share-tech.

item.title: Responsively App
item.description: A dedicated browser for responsive web development — preview a site at multiple screen sizes side by side. Built for faster, more precise responsive work. — shared by UT in #share-tech.

item.title: Grokbot Characters (Rege Lab)
item.description: A Rege Lab page with six little Grokbot character expressions to play with, plus downloadable editable CoAnimato files. A creative asset resource for bot and character design. — shared by Tom in #share-tech.

item.title: Getting the most out of Opus 5.5
item.description: Official Claude guide to prompting Opus 5.5, steering long agent runs, and checking results in Claude apps and Claude Code. A practical reference for anyone driving long agent sessions. — shared by Alp in #share-tech.

item.title: Grokbot Icon Studio
item.description: A minimal bot-icon studio — browse bot icon examples and copy a prompt to generate an icon of your own. Quick asset generation for bot projects. — shared by Tom in #share-tech.

item.title: Cloudflare Quick Tunnels
item.description: Cloudflare Quick Tunnels — free encrypted tunnels that expose localhost as a public URL. Cata plans to use it instead of the VS Code tunnel. — shared by cata in #share-tech.

item.title: BendSR
item.description: Symbolic regression implemented in Bend. A research-flavoured repo for anyone exploring the Bend language. — shared by Tom in #share-tech.

item.title: security-audit-skill
item.description: A coding-agent skill for multi-phase security audits with independently verified, machine-readable findings. A drop-in skill for agentic security reviews. — shared by Alp in #share-tech.

item.title: Saving 100TB of RAM with math
item.description: Cloudflare engineering deep-dive on saving 100TB of RAM with math (and Rust). A solid systems-engineering read. — shared by Rykuuun in #share-tech.

item.title: Bend
item.description: Bend 2 — a fast programming language that blocks AI mistakes via proof checking. Install with curl from bend-lang.com. — shared by Tom in #share-tech.

item.title: Monid free agent search (announcement)
item.description: Announcement of a free agent search/fetch API — "killed Exa, Tavily and Brave", $0 with no quotas, from Tiny_Fish and MonidHQ. The pricing claims are the poster's and unverified; this link is the announcement, not documentation. — shared by Rykuuun in #share-tech.

item.title: jev-search
item.description: Shared by thelaggingway with just "Another one" — context is thin, but it landed in the search-tool thread. Worth a look if you're tracking search APIs. — shared by thelaggingway in #share-tech.

item.title: ArgusAgent
item.description: Microsoft's ArgusAgent — a persistent, reviewed multi-agent runtime for long-horizon research and engineering. Directly relevant to anyone running agents on long tasks. — shared by thelaggingway in #share-tech.

item.title: PrettyMD
item.description: A markdown viewer "for vibe coders" — a simple, beautiful app for reading the .md files your AI writes: specs, plans, skills, agents and more. Pairs naturally with agent-heavy workflows. — shared by Tom in #share-tech.

item.title: LFM2.5-2.6B-RLCD
item.description: LiquidAI's LFM2.5 2.6B model tuned for RLCD, shared in the context of Jev's API and concepts. A small local model for anyone experimenting with RLCD-style agent loops. — shared by Tom in #share-tech.

item.title: Qwen-2.5-1B-RLCD
item.description: A 1B RLCD-tuned Qwen 2.5 that kenn tried locally "to get a feel of how Jev's API and concepts might feel like" — and found it did fine in a roguelike spike. Useful as a tiny testbed model before spending on bigger runs. — shared by kenn in #share-tech.

item.title: Pi coding agent in the browser (announcement)
item.description: Announcement of a coding agent (Pi) running entirely in the browser on a 2B model via WebGPU — MiniCPM5-2B + Pi with Transformers.js and 4-bit ONNX weights. Announcement only; no repo was linked in the post. — shared by asx8678 in #share-tech.

item.title: varve
item.description: An experimental Rust time-series database with DuckDB SQL and tiered Parquet storage — "time settles into layers." Early-stage but interesting for anyone into time-series storage design. — shared by Alp in #share-tech.

item.title: ever-gauzy
item.description: Ever Gauzy — an open business management platform covering ERP, CRM, HRM, ATS and project management (gauzy.co). A full open-source suite if you ever need to stand up business tooling. — shared by Alp in #share-tech.

item.title: Universal syntax highlighter / OpaqueRange (demo)
item.description: Demo of a universal syntax highlighter built on the new OpaqueRange web API (Chrome 152+, 2026) — syntax-highlighting different program fragments efficiently. Worth a look for anyone building code-rendering UI. — shared by Tom in #share-tech.

item.title: The invisible side of design engineering

item.description: The live demo of the snowflow_demo repo below: real-time procedural snow rendering in the browser via WebGPU, Babylon.js, and hand-written WGSL — GPU-generated terrain, snow deformation, procedural characters, cloth, and post-processing with zero textures, meshes, HDRIs, or animation assets. Requires a WebGPU-capable browser (Chrome 113+ on desktop GPU) to load. — shared by Tom in #share-tech.

item.title: snowflow_demo
item.description: Source repo for the Snowflow demo above: a fully procedural real-time snow scene built on WebGPU + Babylon.js with hand-written WGSL shaders — terrain, snow deformation, surf wakes, water spells, atmosphere, and post-processing, all generated at runtime. ~580 stars. — shared by Tom in #share-tech.

item.title: IRIS
item.description: IRIS (Intelligent Real-time Input Suggestion) is an open-source shell auto-completion tool positioned as the successor to Fig: a single native Go binary that runs purely on TTY — no Electron, GUI, account, or telemetry — rendering suggestion menus inline in the real terminal, over SSH and inside tmux. It indexes your aliases and shell history, supports AI suggestions via API key or local models, and configures via a TOML file with instant reload. No Windows support, and it can conflict with other autosuggestion plugins (zsh-autosuggestions, atuin), which the README says to disable first. — shared by formatme in #share-tech.

item.title: kimi-k3-mlx
item.description: An MLX port of moonshotai's Kimi-K3 (2.78T multimodal MoE); the weights are converted from the original release and requantized. Conversion quality is unverified. — shared by JohnDotOwl in #share-tech.

item.title: Hermes Console
item.description: A self-hosted AI agent console ("Tu agente AI self-hosted") that thelaggingway is giving a go. The self-hosted claim is unverified beyond the site's tagline. — shared by thelaggingway in #share-tech.

item.title: OptMem
item.description: Permanent memory for AI agents by Victor Taelin: the whole integration is a 426-token prompt plus a single dependency-free Python script installed with one curl command. You paste a `## Memory` block into your agent's AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, then use `memo wake` (read memory at session start) and `memo note` (record one-liners), plus `nap`, `recall`, `zoom`, and `forget`; storage is an append-only log with a rebuildable binary-tree summary cache (1M memories ≈ 608 MB, wake in 0.03s). — shared by Tom in #share-tech.

item.title: Content Architecture
item.description: A commercial, agent-ready Sanity CMS starter kit in Next.js 16 and Astro 7 editions: a page-builder CMS with in-app Studio, visual editing, draft mode, SEO helpers, a seed dataset, and Plop scaffolding. Its differentiator is agentic-coding workflow support — it ships AGENTS.md plus scoped skills, two preconfigured MCP servers (one reads the running dev server, one drives real Chrome for screenshots/traces), an editable llms.txt, and token-light Markdown versions of every page served to agents via content negotiation. One license per buyer covers unlimited personal, commercial, and client projects; it is a paid product, not open source. — shared by Tom in #share-tech.

item.title: nimbus-lite
item.description: A free, framework-free AI chat UI kit in vanilla HTML/CSS/JS — open index.html and it runs, no build step or dependencies. It includes a full chat layout with sidebar, live token streaming with blinking caret, Markdown plus syntax-highlighted code blocks with copy buttons, a model picker, and light/dark themes with accent colors; it is front-end only, so you bring your own backend (OpenAI, Anthropic, or a local model). The maintainer sells a fuller Nimbus kit ($19) adding citations, reasoning blocks, tool-call chips, and attachments. — shared by Rykuuun in #share-tech.

item.title: worldmonitor
item.description: An open-source (AGPL-3.0) real-time global intelligence dashboard: AI-synthesized news briefs, a 3D globe and WebGL flat map, a live Country Instability Index for 31 Tier-1 countries, and cross-stream correlation of military, economic, and disaster signals. It is built for programmatic access too — MCP server, REST API with OpenAPI spec, CLI (`npx worldmonitor`), and Python/Ruby/Go SDKs, with local-AI support via Ollama — and ships as a web app, Tauri desktop binaries, and PWA. AGPL-3.0 copyleft applies, so commercial/SaaS use needs a separate license or AGPL compliance. — shared by Rykuuun in #share-tech.

item.title: Amicro
item.description: A curated gallery of premium React micro-interaction and transition components built with React and Motion, with layout inspired by transition.dev. It showcases around 36 named interactions — morph, glare shine, magnetic field, text reveal, focus blur, shake, rotate, color-morph buttons — as ready-to-use UI components. Licensing and copy-paste terms are not stated on the page, so reusability is uncertain. — shared by Tom in #share-tech.

item.title: pi-dispatch
item.description: Runs the pi coding agent as a self-hosted background service: triggered on demand, on a cron schedule, or by GitHub/GitLab issues, comments, and pull/merge requests, each job executing in a locked-down ephemeral container with a durable queue. It enforces per-job/daily/weekly/monthly spend caps before a single token is spent, and ships a live admin panel with run history, cost insights, and per-trigger spend analytics; MIT-licensed. Note: the bare npm name `pi-dispatch` belongs to an unrelated package — the scoped `@edgehero/pi-dispatch` is the correct install. — shared by Tom in #share-tech.

item.title: Componentry

item.title: Mint Playground
item.description: The public gallery for Mint's 3D-asset-creation tooling for AI agents: use Codex, Claude, or Cursor (via the Mint MCP server and Mint Skills) to generate, rig, and animate 3D models, build 3D worlds, and create PBR materials and asset packs. The playground showcases dozens of agent-built interactive 3D scenes, from mini-games to product configurators and data visualizations — though it is primarily a showcase for Mint's tooling rather than a tool you operate directly. — shared by Tom in #share-tech.

item.title: delphitools
item.description: A handmade-web collection of small, single-purpose browser tools: colour utilities (contrast checker, palette generator/extractor, Tailwind shade scales), image tools (compressor, converter, background remover, favicon generator, SVG optimiser, metadata stripper), plus audio/video and typography tools. Everything is free with no logins, no paywalls, and no data collection; fully open source (0-BSD), with a native iOS app and an offline CLI offering the same tools. — shared by Tom in #share-tech.

item.title: modly
item.description: An open-source desktop app (Windows, Linux, Apple Silicon macOS) that turns a photo or text prompt into a 3D mesh using open-source AI models running entirely on your own GPU — no cloud inference. It ships an extension system for swapping in models like Hunyuan3D 2 and TripoSG, node-based generation workflows, and a CLI so agents and scripts can drive generation headlessly; MIT-licensed, around 7.7k stars. — shared by Tom in #share-tech.

item.title: img2threejs
item.description: A skill for coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode) that rebuilds the object in a reference photo as a code-only, procedural Three.js model — reconstruction-by-code, not photogrammetry or mesh extraction — with a staged sculpting pipeline (blockout → material → lighting → optimization) and vision-review quality gates. It is deliberately token-efficient: deterministic scripts handle validation while model tokens are spent only on visual judgment and code; Apache 2.0, around 16.7k stars, with a live demo gallery. — shared by Tom in #share-tech.
